first-run: a new project, from kb init to kb stats.

A project directory and some notes written outside it. The store uses the fake embedder
(`fake:8`), so no model is downloaded and the run needs no network.

  $ kb init --model fake:8
  created location $WORK/proj/.kb
  created store "default" in $WORK/proj (model fake:8)

  $ cat .kb/kb.toml
  version = 1
  default_store = "default"

  [aliases]

  $ exists .kb/stores/default/config.toml
  $ exists .kb/stores/default/kb.sqlite
  $ exists data

Add one note by copying it in, then a directory entry (its README.md and docs/*.md).

  $ kb add $WORK/notes/tmux.md
  added data/tmux.md (3 chunks)

  $ kb add --dir $WORK/notes/backup
  added data/backup/README.md (3 chunks)

  $ kb list
  PATH                   SUMMARY                                                    UPDATED     VERIFIED
  data/backup/README.md  How the nightly backup runs and where it writes.           2026-02-02  -
  data/tmux.md           Keep sessions alive after you log out of the remote host.  2026-02-01  -

  2 entries

  $ exists data/tmux.md
  $ exists data/backup/docs/restore.md

Search as a person, then as an agent. Search ids count up, and --json carries the exact
feedback commands for that search.

  $ kb search "tmux logout" --caller claude
  search 1 · 6 hits
  [1] data/tmux.md · updated 2026-02-01
  Tmux survives logout: Keep sessions alive after you log out of the remote host.

  [2] data/tmux.md › Troubleshooting · updated 2026-02-01
  Tmux survives logout › Troubleshooting
  If the session disappears at logout, systemd may be killing user processes. Enable lingering with
  `loginctl enable-linger`.

  [3] data/tmux.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-01
  Tmux survives logout › (intro)
  # Tmux survives logout

  Start `tmux new -s work` on the remote host and detach with Ctrl-b d. The session keeps running
  after logout, and `tmux attach -t work` brings it back.

  [4] data/backup/README.md · updated 2026-02-02
  Nightly backup: How the nightly backup runs and where it writes.

  [5] data/backup/README.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-02
  Nightly backup › Restore from backup › (intro)
  To restore, unpack the newest tarball from the archive volume and run `restore.sh`. Verify the
  restored files before reopening the service.

  [6] data/backup/README.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-02
  Nightly backup › (intro)
  # Nightly backup

  The nightly backup writes a tarball to the archive volume at 02:00 and keeps the last seven.
  search_id=1

  $ kb search "restore the nightly backup" --caller claude --json
  {
    "search_id": 2,
    "feedback": {
      "useful": "kb feedback 2 RANK --useful",
      "not_useful": "kb feedback 2 RANK --not-useful --note \"why\"",
      "none": "kb feedback 2 --none --note \"why\""
    },
    "query": "restore the nightly backup",
    "mode": "hybrid",
    "hits": [
  ...
    ]
  }

Reading a hit is an open of the search that found it, and feedback is a verdict on it.

  $ kb show data/backup/README.md
  ==> data/backup/README.md <==
  ---
  title: Nightly backup
  summary: How the nightly backup runs and where it writes.
  tags: [ops]
  updated: 2026-02-02
  ---
  # Nightly backup

  The nightly backup writes a tarball to the archive volume at 02:00 and keeps the last seven.

  ==> data/backup/docs/restore.md <==
  ---
  title: Restore from backup
  summary: Unpack the newest tarball and run the restore script.
  tags: [ops]
  updated: 2026-02-03
  ---
  # Restore from backup

  To restore, unpack the newest tarball from the archive volume and run `restore.sh`. Verify the
  restored files before reopening the service.

The log now holds three searches, one open and two verdicts. The open counts against the search
that was newest when the entry was read.

An open counts only inside `log.open_window` (30m) of the search. Two hours later, reading the
entry again is not an open of anything, so opened_pct does not move.

  $ env KB_HARNESS_NOW=+2h

  $ kb show data/tmux.md
  ---
  title: Tmux survives logout
  summary: Keep sessions alive after you log out of the remote host.
  tags: [terminal]
  updated: 2026-02-01
  ---
  # Tmux survives logout

  Start `tmux new -s work` on the remote host and detach with Ctrl-b d. The session keeps running
  after logout, and `tmux attach -t work` brings it back.

  ## Troubleshooting

  If the session disappears at logout, systemd may be killing user processes. Enable lingering with
  `loginctl enable-linger`.

-- notes/tmux.md --
---
title: Tmux survives logout
summary: Keep sessions alive after you log out of the remote host.
tags: [terminal]
updated: 2026-02-01
---
# Tmux survives logout

Start `tmux new -s work` on the remote host and detach with Ctrl-b d. The session keeps running
after logout, and `tmux attach -t work` brings it back.

## Troubleshooting

If the session disappears at logout, systemd may be killing user processes. Enable lingering with
`loginctl enable-linger`.
